note: Claims a story makes. A quantitative claim names the tokens it fills, the model state that produces them and its limitations; its numbers are computed on the page from that state, never stored here (docs/civic/editorial-policy.md).

claims.text: At the 100-year storm tide (9.73 ft NAVD88 still water), {{wetLandHa}} ha of Berkeley land is under Bay water connected over the ground, and {{lowLandHa}} ha lies below the level with no surface path to the Bay.
limitations: Connected fill on bare-earth lidar (4 m grid), with no waves, groundwater, duration or flow.
Ground with no surface path to the Bay floods only if water reaches it another way.

claims.text: With every modeled outfall open, {{drainLandHa}} ha of cut-off ground holding a storm drain inlet could fill through the drains at the 100-year storm tide ({{drainByWatershed}}).
limitations: Upper bound: every inlet is assumed to connect to an open outfall, and the tide to last long enough to fill the pipes.
Outfall locations are modeled from watershed outlines.
Which outfalls have tide gates is unpublished.

claims.text: With tide gates modeled closed on every outfall but the Aquatic Park tide tubes, ground that can fill up the drains at the 100-year storm tide falls from {{baseDrainLandHa}} ha to {{drainLandHa}} ha, {{aquaticParkDrainHa}} ha of it in the Aquatic Park watershed, whose drains empty into the lagoon.
limitations: The two runs bracket the real drains, whose gates are unpublished.
The lagoon is assumed to follow the Bay's level; five 24-inch tubes may hold it lower through a short tide (D9).

claims.text: A 10-year, 6-hour storm ({{rainDepthIn}} in, NOAA Atlas 14) with all runoff held back by closed outfalls pools on {{rainLandHa}} ha of Berkeley land in this model, at the 100-year storm tide.
limitations: Each watershed's runoff pools at its lowest inlet, which can overstate depth there and miss ponding elsewhere.
The share of rain that cannot drain (here 100%) is a setting.
The Simple Method runoff share is applied beyond the drainage areas it was made for.
